about.body: The N57 is BMW's 3.0-litre turbocharged inline-six diesel engine, produced from 2008 to 2019. It was the successor to the M57 and served as BMW's flagship diesel six-cylinder across the 3, 4, 5 and 6 Series, plus the X3, X4, X5, X6 and X7 SUV range — before being phased out in favour of the B57 from 2015 onwards (the B57 is the newer modular engine family, though the N57 continued to appear in some applications through 2019).

byModel.body: Across the 3 Series, the N57 powered the 330d and 335d (F30/F31) from 2012 to 2019. The 4 Series followed with the 430d and 435d (F32/F33/F36) from 2013 to 2019. The 5 Series used it in the 530d and 535d (F10/F11) from 2010 to 2017. The 6 Series carried it in the 630d and 640d (F06/F12/F13) during its final generation. Across the SUV range, the N57 appeared in the X4 (F26), X5 (F15) and X6 (F16) — each available with both the xDrive30d and xDrive35d/xDrive40d variants.

compatibility.body: Because the N57 spans 7 different models across multiple generations, compatibility comes down to confirming your exact model, generation, and drivetrain spec, which we do by registration. Ancillaries, mounting, and ECU/DME software all differ by application — an N57 from a 3 Series isn't a drop-in match for one from an X5, even though the base engine code is the same. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm your exact vehicle.
